answer: 5371 project-local callables open a file and they sit on up to 86616 site lines the stdlib table reads as 'other', but every key they open is opened by a stdlib call somewhere too, so no published key class moves: the keys named only by non-opening sites stay at 1 of 883.  The residue is a cohort, not a hidden file reader: of the 10 sites the stdlib table calls 'other', 10 are git-object reads (`git show`/`cat-file` through subprocess, 63 such helpers), so no table of file-opening callables could ever classify them; they span 4 keys and 1 key is named only that way

bounds.measured: every def's direct callees; a helper inherits a kind from a local callee for at most 4 hops; each key literal is classified by E384's own io_map run twice -- once unpatched, once with the helper names added; the git-object arm is measured by an argv literal carrying a git subcommand
bounds.no_rewrites: no published face, reader or caller is edited; e384.classify_call is restored
bounds.not_measured: dispatch through getattr/decorators/imported helpers outside the corpus; a name defined in several modules is merged by name, so a site is attributed to the union of that name's definitions -- which makes the moved-site count an upper bound and is why no key class moves on it
